items.title: UI wiring canon and autonomous verification authority
items.statement: This document is the canonical owner for GUI-to-backend wiring rules, and every rule is required to be verifiable with schema validation, deterministic lints, and scriptable checks without paid UI tooling.

evidence.exact_quote: This file is the canonical SSOT for UI wiring rules that guarantee the Puppet Master GUI is fully wired to backend behavior.
All rules in this document are autonomously verifiable without paid UI tooling; verification relies exclusively on schema validation, deterministic lints, and scriptable checks.

items.title: Concept artifacts are lineage inputs, not canon
items.statement: The designated HTML concept artifacts guide reconciliation and wiring review but are not live Plans owners and cannot be copied verbatim into canon; UI wiring, layout, and command truth remain in their named owner documents.

evidence.exact_quote: When a GUI concept artifact is included in a reconciliation packet, `Concepts/PuppetMasterDashComp.html` is the primary concept input for wiring review until superseded by a newer explicit concept artifact in the same packet. The path token `/PuppetMasterDashComp.html` is evidence lineage, not a live Plans owner path; UI wiring canon remains in this document, GUI product/layout canon remains in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md`, and command canon remains in `Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md`.

`Concepts/PMConcept.html` is likewise a GUI concept-lineage input when cited by a transfer source; `/PMConcept.html` drives reconciliation targeting and wiring review but MUST NOT be copied verbatim into canon or treated as a live owner path.

items.title: Production status requires complete concept-control wiring
items.statement: A PMConcept control remains lineage-only until it has production command, state, handler, receipt, and test coverage; concept-local demo or mock data remains fixture-only until replaced by a canonical projected-state contract.

evidence.exact_quote: For the 2026-07-02 GUI/PMConcept readiness repair, `Plans/PMConcept_Control_Reconciliation.json` is the machine-readable concept reconciliation artifact and `Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json` is the schema-validated production wiring artifact. PMConcept controls without production command/state/handler/receipt/test coverage remain concept lineage only. PMConcept local/demo/mock data is `concept_fixture_only` unless a canonical owner doc replaces it with a real projected state contract.

items.title: Accessibility and interaction readiness are GATE-010 obligations
items.statement: Every retained actionable control must prove naming, role, keyboard activation, focus behavior, applicable state semantics, disabled-reason projection, command binding, handler target, receipt/event effect, and test evidence; the listed accessibility omissions are GATE-010 failures.

evidence.exact_quote: Production wiring evidence MUST include accessibility and interaction readiness: every retained actionable control has an accessible name, semantic role, keyboard activation contract, focus behavior, state attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`, or equivalent native state where applicable), disabled reason projection, UICommand binding, handler target, receipt/event effect, and test evidence. Icon-only controls without names, custom clickable elements without keyboard parity, tab/menu/disclosure controls without state semantics, and disabled controls without user-visible reasons are GATE-010 failures.

items.title: Annotation wiring spans reusable components and review surfaces
items.statement: Annotation and targeted revision must wire the named reusable components, commands, projected state, live-region/status updates, and distinct send-to-chat chip behavior across all four named review surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: Annotation and targeted-revision work is a cross-surface GUI feature, not just a backend `note-schema` tweak. Wiring must cover the reusable GUI components in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` (`AnnotationActionMenu`, `AnnotationDrawer`, `ContextChipStrip`), their commands, projected state, status/live-region updates, and separate send-to-chat chip behavior across Assistant Deep Plan, Wizard/PRD review, Interview embedded document pane, and document viewer review surfaces.

items.title: Route-aware metadata proves but does not own route semantics
items.statement: Route-aware wiring can add the named proof metadata while remaining a consumer of route/open semantics. Usage route/open rows additionally require route target, OpenSubject, usage-event object identity when applicable, and UsageRecord/runtime/provider reference passthrough.

evidence.exact_quote: Route-aware wiring verification extends the simple `ui_element_id -> ui_command_id -> handler_location -> expected_event_types` proof with optional metadata fields: `command_arg_contract_ref?`, `route_target_kind?`, `subject_kind?`, `deprecated_alias_for?`, `preconditions?`, `arg_passthrough_requirements?`, `correlation_passthrough?`, and `route_contract?`. For Usage route/open rows, `route_contract` is a validation proof packet: it requires `route_target`, `OpenSubject`, `route_target.object_kind = usage_event` when `usage_event_ref` exists, and passthrough for UsageRecord/runtime/provider refs. These fields are verification hints only; `WiringEntry` consumes route/open semantics and cannot become the route owner.

items.title: GATE-010 verifies normalized route dispatch
items.statement: Route-aware GATE-010 evidence must cover schema validity, command and handler resolution, expected event emission, unknown-command rejection, architecture, wrapper normalization, argument and correlation passthrough, and target-kind checks.

evidence.exact_quote: `GATE-010` route-aware verification includes schema validation, command coverage, handler resolution, `expected-event` emission, unknown-command rejection, architectural lints, wrapper normalization, argument passthrough, correlation passthrough, and route target kind checks.

items.title: Runtime actions normalize to canonical runtime commands
items.statement: Legacy graph recovery actions normalize to the canonical runtime command family, and package, lane, and package/lane promotion controls must dispatch cataloged command IDs rather than ad hoc confirms or untyped shortcuts.

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime action wiring reconciles old `cmd.graph` / `cmd.graph.*` recovery actions to canonical `cmd.runtime` / `cmd.runtime.*` command contracts. Package, lane, and `/package/lane` promotion controls must dispatch through cataloged command IDs rather than ad hoc UI confirms or untyped wiring shortcuts.

items.title: Reserved command overrides require catalog resolution
items.statement: The reserved chat and orchestrator families must be cataloged before wiring lands; every referenced but uncataloged identifier remains a gate failure until cataloged, aliased, or retired.

evidence.exact_quote: Reserved slash-command override policy must resolve into one command-catalog rule: real `cmd.chat`, `cmd.chat.*`, `cmd.orchestrator`, and `cmd.orchestrator.*` IDs must be cataloged before UI wiring lands, and referenced-but-uncataloged IDs such as `cmd.chat.run_user_command`, `cmd.orchestrator.switch_tab`, and `cmd.chat.branch_from_restore` remain gate failures until cataloged, aliased, or retired.

items.title: Element-command-handler-event rows remain the baseline proof
items.statement: The machine-readable matrix remains interactive-element dispatch rows proving element-to-command-to-handler-to-event coverage; route and producer/consumer trace proof is layered above, not substituted for, that row shape.

evidence.exact_quote: Element-centric and command-centric wiring remains the baseline proof: `ui_element_id -> ui_command_id -> handler_location -> expected_event_types` proves dispatch coverage, while route-aware gates add navigation, subject, and `/consumer/runtime-trace` checks without replacing the row shape. The machine-readable wiring schema remains a set of `interactive-element` dispatch rows; producer/consumer trace evidence is layered above that schema rather than used as a substitute for it.

items.title: UICommand envelope fields remain visible and pass through
items.statement: Wiring evidence must keep the five named UICommand envelope fields visible and may verify their passthrough without redefining the command contract.

evidence.exact_quote: The UI command envelope evidence keeps `command_id`, `issued_at`, `origin`, `correlation_id`, and `args` visible and references `Contracts_V0.md`; wiring rows may verify envelope passthrough but do not redefine the command contract.

items.title: Wrapper commands normalize to shared route primitives
items.statement: A public navigation command family is optional alias surface; wrapper commands must normalize to shared route primitives, and any navigation prototype carries deprecation, registration, and gate-maintenance obligations.

evidence.exact_quote: A broad public `cmd.nav` / `cmd.nav.*` family is optional alias surface, not the mandatory answer for every route. Wrapper commands can normalize to shared route contracts, and any `cmd.nav` prototype must carry alias `/deprecation`, handler-registration, and gate-maintenance consequences through `GATE-010`.

`GATE-010` must verify that wrapper command IDs normalize to shared route primitives instead of treating every public command ID as independent. Generalized route `/subject` navigation cannot be reduced to one-off handler/event coverage; the gate evidence must prove argument passthrough, subject kind, route target kind, and wrapper normalization.

items.title: Compatibility and availability boundaries are explicit
items.statement: Stale Tiers vocabulary is lineage-only, action availability blockers remain owner-doc issues rather than cosmetic prose drift, and adjacent account-usage controls cannot be exposed until their command and effective-account contract exists.

evidence.exact_quote: Stale `Tiers` vocabulary from `FinalGUISpec.md` is compatibility lineage only; wiring rules do not reintroduce `Tiers` as a live route, object, or navigation vocabulary.

Wiring SSOT / SSOTs integrity includes stale or `/degraded` action preconditions, owner-doc `/runtime` gating, dispatcher/runtime gating, and command registration. These are owner-doc blocking issues when they affect action availability; they are not cosmetic drift in wiring prose.

Adjacent `GUI` usage controls such as `auth-mode` and `/effective-account` filtering remain consumer requirements until usage/account owners guarantee them. UI wiring may expose the `/UI` control only when the command and effective-account contract exists.

items.title: Owner and consumer boundaries are enumerated
items.statement: This document owns UI-side dispatcher boundaries, wiring-row expectations, and autonomous coverage verification while consuming command, envelope, visible behavior, and gate contracts; layout, command membership, runtime schemas, routes, storage, and evidence schemas remain external owners.

evidence.exact_quote: This document owns UI wiring rules, dispatcher boundary requirements from the UI side, wiring matrix row expectations, and autonomous verification strategy for interactive GUI command coverage. It consumes command identifiers from `Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md`, command and event envelope contracts from `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`, GUI placement and visible behavior from `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md`, and gate definitions from `Plans/Progression_Gates.md`.

This document does not own product layout, command catalog membership, runtime event schemas, route semantics, storage projections, or evidence bundle schemas. Those remain with their owner docs and are referenced here for wiring verification.

items.title: View layer dispatches typed commands only
items.statement: Every user-initiated UI interaction emits a typed, cataloged UICommand; the view is a pure projected-state function and cannot directly call or retain backend services, storage, domain logic, handlers, or services.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The UI layer MUST dispatch only typed UICommand messages with stable command_id values from Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md. The view layer is a pure function of projected state plus outbound UICommand emissions and MUST NOT call backend services, storage, domain logic, handlers, or services directly.
- User-initiated UI interactions emit typed UICommand envelopes.

items.title: Every interactive element maps to exactly one command
items.statement: Each button, menu item, link, toggle, slider, and form submit must have exactly one Wiring Matrix command mapping, and each catalog command must have handler registration; either orphan condition fails verification.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Every interactive UI element, including buttons, menu items, links, toggles, sliders, and form submits, MUST map to exactly one UICommandID recorded in the Wiring Matrix. Orphan elements and orphan commands are gate failures.
- Every UICommandID has a handler registration.

items.title: Dispatch flow terminates in projected UI state
items.statement: The required propagation is UI element to command envelope to dispatcher to stateless handler to event record to projection to UI state, preserving command_id, args, and correlation_id; an unknown command produces a structured error and no domain event.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI command dispatch flows from UI Element to UICommand envelope to Dispatcher to Handler to EventRecord to Projection to UI State. The dispatcher rejects unknown command_id values with structured errors, handlers remain UI-stateless, and UI/view code observes projected state rather than mutating domain state.
- UI command flow preserves command_id, args, and correlation_id through dispatch.
- Unknown command_id values return structured errors and emit no domain events.

items.title: Wiring Matrix row and storage shape are fixed
items.statement: The matrix binds every interactive element to handler and expected-outcome evidence with the seven named row fields, stored under entries as a map keyed by ui_element_id; lifecycle, storage, and runtime canon stay in owner docs.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The Wiring Matrix binds every interactive UI element to command handler and expected outcome evidence. Rows include ui_element_id, ui_location, ui_command_id, handler_location, expected_event_types, acceptance_checks, and evidence_required, with machine-readable entries keyed by ui_element_id.
- Wiring Matrix JSON stores rows under entries as a map keyed by ui_element_id.

items.title: Autonomous verification blocks progression without override
items.statement: The verification suite includes the nine named checks, runs without paid tooling or manual inspection, emits evidence conforming to the evidence schema, and blocks progression on any GATE-010 failure with no manual override.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI wiring verification is scriptable and includes schema validation, element uniqueness, command coverage, handler registration, event emission tests, unknown-command rejection tests, handler statelessness lint, UI purity checks, and dead command detection. GATE-010 failures block progression with no manual override.
- Evidence bundles produced by checks conform to Plans/evidence.schema.json.
- No manual override is permitted for gate failure.

items.title: Reference boundaries remain lintable without owner duplication
items.statement: The wiring canon references the named contract, architecture, gate, matrix, evidence, DRY, and decision owners, while reference rows must remain exact for lint and migration coverage and must not restate competing owner prose.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI wiring references Contracts_V0, UI_Command_Catalog, Architecture_Invariants, Progression_Gates, Wiring_Matrix, Wiring_Matrix.schema.json, evidence.schema.json, DRY_Rules, and Decision_Policy while preserving their owner boundaries.
- UI wiring does not restate owner-doc contracts beyond what is needed for wiring verification.

items.statement: The document requires every rule to be autonomously script-verifiable but names only future UI wiring verifier scripts for the comprehensive suite, leaving the current executable entry point and complete check implementation unspecified within this wiring contract.

items.statement: The route-aware fields are labeled optional and Usage receives one specific route_contract rule, but the contract does not define which non-Usage route or command classes require each field or when omission is valid.

These fields are verification hints only; `WiringEntry` consumes route/open semantics and cannot become the route owner.

items.impact: Two conforming builders can produce different route proof coverage and different GATE-010 outcomes for the same non-Usage row.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must infer applicability from external owner contracts without a deterministic row-class-to-required-field rule here.

items.title: Visible command evidence has no privacy or redaction rule
items.statement: The wiring contract requires args and correlation identifiers to remain visible in evidence but does not specify redaction, classification, access, or retention behavior when those fields contain sensitive values.

evidence.exact_quote: The UI command envelope evidence keeps `command_id`, `issued_at`, `origin`, `correlation_id`, and `args` visible and references `Contracts_V0.md`; wiring rows may verify envelope passthrough but do not redefine the command contract.

items.impact: Verification evidence can expose command arguments or correlators unless an external contract supplies safeguards that this wiring requirement explicitly consumes and tests.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose whether and how to redact or restrict evidence while still satisfying the word visible.

items.title: Gate operations and recovery ownership are unspecified
items.statement: The suite and blocking policy are listed, but this document does not state when the full suite runs, where its authoritative result is written, who owns restoring a failed gate, or how a corrected run supersedes a prior failure.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI wiring verification is scriptable and includes schema validation, element uniqueness, command coverage, handler registration, event emission tests, unknown-command rejection tests, handler statelessness lint, UI purity checks, and dead command detection. GATE-010 failures block progression with no manual override.

items.title: No scale or performance oracle exists for wiring dispatch and verification
items.statement: The contract fixes matrix shape and required checks but gives no dispatch latency, verification duration, matrix-size, batching, or resource budget by which behavior at production scale can be accepted or rejected.

Rows include ui_element_id, ui_location, ui_command_id, handler_location, expected_event_types, acceptance_checks, and evidence_required, with machine-readable entries keyed by ui_element_id.

items.title: Equivalent native accessibility state is not mapped
items.statement: The accessibility rule permits an equivalent native state where applicable but does not define the control categories, native state equivalents, or test assertions that make that substitution deterministic.

evidence.exact_quote: Production wiring evidence MUST include accessibility and interaction readiness: every retained actionable control has an accessible name, semantic role, keyboard activation contract, focus behavior, state attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`, or equivalent native state where applicable), disabled reason projection, UICommand binding, handler target, receipt/event effect, and test evidence. Icon-only controls without names, custom clickable elements without keyboard parity, tab/menu/disclosure controls without state semantics, and disabled controls without user-visible reasons are GATE-010 failures.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree about whether a native control proves the required state semantics, producing inconsistent GATE-010 results.

items.title: Unknown-command UI recovery behavior is not wired
items.statement: Unknown commands are required to return structured errors without domain events, but the wiring contract does not specify the projected error state, user-visible presentation, retry or dismissal behavior, or correlation of that failure back to the originating control.

evidence.exact_quote: - Unknown command_id values return structured errors and emit no domain events.

items.impact: Backend rejection is deterministic, but the GUI can silently fail or present incompatible recovery experiences while satisfying the stated dispatcher test.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent the failure projection and interaction recovery path.

dimension_assessments.summary: Typed dispatch, cross-surface annotation behavior, command normalization, wrapper normalization, and end-to-end command flow are explicitly prescribed.
The wiring layer can reconcile concept controls, prove production coverage, bind matrix rows, and autonomously gate progression.
Command envelope inputs, handler/event outputs, projected state, and matrix evidence fields are named.
Concept production status, route proof, command catalog membership, typed dispatch, row shape, and reference boundaries are contractually constrained.
The element-to-projection transition chain, projected-state-only UI rule, and unknown-command no-event branch are explicit.
Canonical wiring authority and external product, command, runtime, route, storage, and evidence authorities are separated.
The owner/consumer map and negative owner boundaries are explicit down to route and evidence semantics.
Command, contract, GUI, gate, matrix, runtime-artifact, and usage/account relationships identify both consumed owners and downstream consumers.
Concept lineage is distinguished from production truth, control readiness is gated, and accessibility plus projected-state behavior are required.
Unknown-command rejection and gate blocking are specified, but user-visible unknown-command recovery and gate rerun/remediation lifecycle are not.
Visible command args and correlators have no local evidence redaction, access, classification, or retention contract.
Argument, correlation, subject, route target, event, and projection propagation are named and gate-verifiable.
A blocking check suite and evidence schema are named, but the current full-suite command, trigger cadence, result location, rerun semantics, and recovery owner are not.
No dispatch or verification performance budget, size limit, or production-scale oracle is stated.
Legacy graph commands, optional navigation aliases, stale Tiers vocabulary, deprecation consequences, and migration coverage are explicitly bounded.
GATE-010 and its checks are strong oracles, but the comprehensive current executable entry point and native accessibility equivalence mapping are incomplete.
Builders retain consequential discretion over route metadata applicability, evidence privacy, gate operations, performance budgets, native state equivalents, and UI recovery.

The principal unknowns are current verifier implementation, optional metadata applicability, privacy handling, operational lifecycle, native-state equivalence, and unknown-command recovery projection.
